```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 7)
```

A gq web map takes four calls. `gq_mapgl_basemap()` starts the map on a basemap
fitted to the data. `gq_mapgl_network()` adds lakes and streams styled from the
registry, with streams drawn wider by stream order. `gq_mapgl_layer()` adds each
layer with its legend, and `gq_mapgl_controls()` adds a switch for the layers,
zoom buttons and a scale bar. Each legend is tied to its layer, so switching a
layer off hides its legend too.

Both maps below are drawn in a subbasin of the Neexdzii Kwa (Upper Bulkley
River), between Johnny David Creek and Richfield Creek, with the data bundled
in gq.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(gq)
library(sf)
sf_use_s2(FALSE)
reg <- gq_reg_main()
```

## Where has each salmon and trout been recorded?

One layer per species makes each one a switch. The colours are named here
because the registry styles fish observations as one layer, not by species.

```{r species, fig.cap = "Fish observations of salmon, trout and char in the Neexdzii Kwa subbasin, one layer per species. Use the switch at the top right to show one species at a time. Observations at one site sit on top of each other, so switch a species off to see the ones beneath. Other species recorded here are left out.", fig.alt = "Interactive map of the Neexdzii Kwa subbasin with streams, lakes and fish observations coloured by species, a legend at the top left and a layer switch at the top right"}
species <- c(RB = "rainbow trout", BT = "bull trout", CO = "coho", DV = "Dolly Varden",
             CH = "chinook", ST = "steelhead", CT = "cutthroat trout")
colours <- c(RB = "#377EB8", BT = "#E41A1C", CO = "#FF7F00", DV = "#984EA3",
             CH = "#4DAF4A", ST = "#A65628", CT = "#F781BF")
outline <- st_cast(neexdzii_wsd, "MULTILINESTRING")

m <- gq_mapgl_basemap(neexdzii_wsd, "positron") |>
  gq_mapgl_network(streams = neexdzii_streams["stream_order"],
                   water = neexdzii_lakes["gnis_name_1"], reg = reg, legend = TRUE) |>
  gq_mapgl_layer("subbasin", outline, color = "#2c3e50", width = 1.5, legend = FALSE)

for (code in names(species)) {
  obs <- neexdzii_fish_obs[neexdzii_fish_obs$species_code == code,
                           c("observation_date", "life_stage")]
  pop <- gq_mapgl_popup(obs, c(Recorded = "observation_date", "Life stage" = "life_stage"))
  m <- gq_mapgl_layer(m, species[[code]], pop$data, color = colours[[code]], radius = 6,
                      popup = pop$expr, circle_stroke_color = "#ffffff",
                      circle_stroke_width = 1)
}

gq_mapgl_controls(m, unname(species))
```

The popup is built by `gq_mapgl_popup()`. It writes a missing value as `none`,
and the browser assembles each popup from the columns, which keeps the page
small.

## A classified layer from the registry

A registry key draws a layer in the registry's classes, with one legend row
per class. Here the crossings are coloured by barrier status. Their data names
the column `barrier_status` where the registry names it `barrier_result_code`,
so `field` says which column to read.

```{r crossings, message = FALSE, fig.cap = "Assessed stream crossings in the Neexdzii Kwa subbasin, coloured by barrier status from the gq registry. The 130 crossings that are modelled but not yet assessed are left out. Click a crossing for its stream and type.", fig.alt = "Interactive map of the Neexdzii Kwa subbasin with assessed stream crossings coloured as barrier, passable or unknown"}
assessed <- neexdzii_crossings[neexdzii_crossings$barrier_status != "POTENTIAL",
                               c("barrier_status", "gnis_stream_name", "crossing_type_code")]
pop <- gq_mapgl_popup(assessed, c(Status = "barrier_status", Stream = "gnis_stream_name",
                                  Type = "crossing_type_code"))

gq_mapgl_basemap(neexdzii_wsd, "positron") |>
  gq_mapgl_network(streams = neexdzii_streams["stream_order"],
                   water = neexdzii_lakes["gnis_name_1"], reg = reg, legend = TRUE) |>
  gq_mapgl_layer("subbasin", outline, color = "#2c3e50", width = 1.5, legend = FALSE) |>
  gq_mapgl_layer("crossings", pop$data, key = "crossings_pscis_assessment", reg = reg,
                 field = "barrier_status", legend_title = "Barrier status",
                 popup = pop$expr, circle_stroke_color = "#ffffff",
                 circle_stroke_width = 1) |>
  gq_mapgl_controls(c("Assessed crossings" = "crossings"))
```

```{r crossings-note, include = FALSE}
# message = FALSE above: mapgl stores a named layer switch as a named vector, and
# jsonlite says, when the page is written, that it will one day serialise named
# vectors as arrays. The map is correct today; the message is mapgl's to answer.
```

## What the web map does not draw

The registry carries more than MapLibre draws through these helpers. A
classified line layer draws every class at one width and with no dashes, and a
point layer draws as circles whatever shape the registry gives it. The static
maps from `gq_tmap_style()` draw both.
